## Simple graph

```{r simple}

g_no_loop <- make_graph(
  ~ A--B,
  A--C,
  B--C,
  B--D,
  C--E,
  D--E
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate the layout once from the graph without the loop (for later use)


set.seed(123)

xy <- layout_with_fr(g_no_loop)

# Plot the graph

p_no_loop <- ggraph(
  g_no_loop,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy[, 1],
  y = xy[, 2]
) +
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  theme_void()

p_no_loop
```


# Graphs continued 


```{r }
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create the original undirected simple graph
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_no_loop <- make_graph(
  ~ A--B,
    A--C,
    B--C,
    B--D,
    C--E,
    D--E
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate the original layout for vertices A to E
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

xy <- layout_with_fr(g_no_loop)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Add vertices F and G
#
# F is a pendant vertex connected only to E.
# G is an isolated vertex.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_extended <- add_vertices(
  g_no_loop,
  nv = 2,
  name = c("F", "G")
)

g_extended <- add_edges(
  g_extended,
  c("E", "F")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Preserve the original positions of A to E
#
# F is placed close to E.
# G is placed halfway between C and F.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

E_row <- which(V(g_no_loop)$name == "E")
C_row <- which(V(g_no_loop)$name == "C")

F_xy <- xy[E_row, ] + c(0.8, -0.4)

G_xy <- (xy[C_row, ] + F_xy) / 2

xy_extended <- rbind(
  xy,
  F_xy,
  G_xy
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot the extended graph without a loop
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_extended <- ggraph(
  g_extended,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy_extended[, 1],
  y = xy_extended[, 2]
) +
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  theme_void()

p_extended

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Copy the extended graph and add a self-loop to B
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_with_loop <- g_extended

B_id <- as.integer(
  V(g_with_loop)["B"]
)

g_with_loop <- add_edges(
  g_with_loop,
  c(B_id, B_id)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Plot the graph with the loop using the same layout
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_with_loop <- ggraph(
  g_with_loop,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy_extended[, 1],
  y = xy_extended[, 2]
) +
  
  # Draw the ordinary edges
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Draw the self-loop separately
  geom_edge_loop(
    aes(
      direction = 140,
      span = 100,
      strength = 1.5
    ),
    colour = "#D95F02",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  
  # Draw vertices over the edges
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  
  # Vertex labels
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  
  coord_equal(
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  theme_void()

p_with_loop

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Verify the graph structure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

as_edgelist(
  g_with_loop,
  names = TRUE
)

which_loop(g_with_loop)

degree(g_with_loop)

# ----------
```


## Directed and mixed graphs

```{r}
# graph is created as directed, direction plotted selectively to make the example...
# Install patchwork first if necessary:
# install.packages("patchwork")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define vertices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vertices <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create the original undirected simple graph
# ------------------------------------------------------------

undirected_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "D"),
  to   = c("B", "C", "C", "D", "E", "E")
)

g_undirected <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = undirected_edges,
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate one fixed layout
#
# This layout is reused in all three panels.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

xy <- layout_with_fr(g_undirected)

# Store coordinates together with vertex names
layout_fixed <- data.frame(
  name = V(g_undirected)$name,
  x = xy[, 1],
  y = xy[, 2]
)

# Ensure coordinates follow the same vertex order in each graph
get_coordinates <- function(graph, layout_data) {
  
  matched_rows <- match(
    V(graph)$name,
    layout_data$name
  )
  
  as.matrix(
    layout_data[matched_rows, c("x", "y")]
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Create the directed graph
#
# Directions:
# A -> B
# C -> A
# B -> C
# D -> B
# C -> E
# E -> D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

directed_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "C", "B", "D", "C", "E"),
  to   = c("B", "A", "C", "B", "E", "D")
)

g_directed <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = directed_edges,
  directed = TRUE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Define the mixed graph
#
# Undirected edges:
# A -- C
# B -- C
# C -- E
#
# Directed edges:
# A -> B
# B -> D
# E -> D
#
# The two edge types are plotted using separate graph objects.
# This avoids treating the entire mixed graph as either
# uniformly directed or uniformly undirected.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

mixed_undirected_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "B", "C"),
  to   = c("C", "C", "E")
)

mixed_directed_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "B", "E"),
  to   = c("B", "D", "D")
)

g_mixed_undirected <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = mixed_undirected_edges,
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = vertices
)

g_mixed_directed <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = mixed_directed_edges,
  directed = TRUE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Extract coordinates in the correct order for each graph
# ------------------------------------------------------------

xy_undirected <- get_coordinates(
  g_undirected,
  layout_fixed
)

xy_directed <- get_coordinates(
  g_directed,
  layout_fixed
)

xy_mixed_undirected <- get_coordinates(
  g_mixed_undirected,
  layout_fixed
)

xy_mixed_directed <- get_coordinates(
  g_mixed_directed,
  layout_fixed
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Define common coordinate limits
#
# Identical limits ensure equal scaling in all three panels.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

x_limits <- range(layout_fixed$x)
y_limits <- range(layout_fixed$y)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Plot 1: undirected graph
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_undirected <- ggraph(
  g_undirected,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy_undirected[, 1],
  y = xy_undirected[, 2]
) +
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = x_limits,
    ylim = y_limits,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Undirected graph"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Plot 2: directed graph
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_directed <- ggraph(
  g_directed,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy_directed[, 1],
  y = xy_directed[, 2]
) +
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    arrow = arrow(
      type = "closed",
      length = unit(3.5, "mm")
    ),
    start_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    ),
    end_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    )
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = x_limits,
    ylim = y_limits,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Directed graph"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Plot 3: mixed graph
#
# First construct an empty plot with the fixed node layout.
# Then add the undirected and directed edges as separate layers.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

mixed_undirected_edge_data <- get_edges()(
  create_layout(
    g_mixed_undirected,
    layout = "manual",
    x = xy_mixed_undirected[, 1],
    y = xy_mixed_undirected[, 2]
  )
)

mixed_directed_edge_data <- get_edges()(
  create_layout(
    g_mixed_directed,
    layout = "manual",
    x = xy_mixed_directed[, 1],
    y = xy_mixed_directed[, 2]
  )
)

p_mixed <- ggraph(
  g_undirected,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy_undirected[, 1],
  y = xy_undirected[, 2]
) +
  
  # Undirected edges
  geom_edge_link(
    data = mixed_undirected_edge_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      xend = xend,
      yend = yend,
      group = edge.id
    ),
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # Directed edges
  geom_edge_link(
    data = mixed_directed_edge_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      xend = xend,
      yend = yend,
      group = edge.id
    ),
    colour = "#D95F02",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    arrow = arrow(
      type = "closed",
      length = unit(3.5, "mm")
    ),
    start_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    ),
    end_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = x_limits,
    ylim = y_limits,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mixed graph"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Combine the three graphs side by side
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_combined <- p_undirected +
  p_directed +
  p_mixed +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 3
  )

p_combined

p_combined2 <- p_undirected +
  p_directed +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 1
  )

p_combined2

```


## shortest path


```{r}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the common vertex set
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vertices <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create the original undirected simple graph
# ------------------------------------------------------------

undirected_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "D"),
  to   = c("B", "C", "C", "D", "E", "E")
)

g_undirected <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = undirected_edges,
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate one fixed layout
#
# The same coordinates are used for both graphs.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(123)

xy <- layout_with_fr(g_undirected)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Find the shortest undirected path from A to D
#
# The expected path is:
# A -- B -- D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

shortest_undirected <- shortest_paths(
  g_undirected,
  from = "A",
  to = "D",
  output = "both"
)

undirected_path_vertices <- shortest_undirected$vpath[[1]]
undirected_path_edges <- shortest_undirected$epath[[1]]

# Mark edges belonging to the shortest path
E(g_undirected)$on_shortest_path <- FALSE

E(g_undirected)$on_shortest_path[
  as.integer(undirected_path_edges)
] <- TRUE

# Display the path in the R console
V(g_undirected)$name[
  as.integer(undirected_path_vertices)
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create the directed graph
#
# Directions:
# A -> B
# C -> A
# B -> C
# D -> B
# C -> E
# E -> D
#
# The directed path from A to D is:
# A -> B -> C -> E -> D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

directed_edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "C", "B", "D", "C", "E"),
  to   = c("B", "A", "C", "B", "E", "D")
)

g_directed <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = directed_edges,
  directed = TRUE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Find the shortest directed path from A to D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

shortest_directed <- shortest_paths(
  g_directed,
  from = "A",
  to = "D",
  mode = "out",
  output = "both"
)

directed_path_vertices <- shortest_directed$vpath[[1]]
directed_path_edges <- shortest_directed$epath[[1]]

# Mark arcs belonging to the shortest directed path
E(g_directed)$on_shortest_path <- FALSE

E(g_directed)$on_shortest_path[
  as.integer(directed_path_edges)
] <- TRUE

# Display the directed path in the R console
V(g_directed)$name[
  as.integer(directed_path_vertices)
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Define common coordinate ranges
# ------------------------------------------------------------

x_limits <- range(xy[, 1])
y_limits <- range(xy[, 2])

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Plot the undirected graph
#
# Grey edges are not part of the shortest path.
# Orange edges form the shortest path A -- B -- D.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_undirected_path <- ggraph(
  g_undirected,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy[, 1],
  y = xy[, 2]
) +
  
  # All edges in grey
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey75",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Shortest-path edges in orange
  geom_edge_link(
    aes(
      filter = on_shortest_path
    ),
    colour = "#D95F02",
    linewidth = 1.8
  ) +
  
  # Vertices
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  
  # Vertex labels
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  
  coord_equal(
    xlim = x_limits,
    ylim = y_limits,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Undirected graph",
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      colour = "#D95F02",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Plot the directed graph
#
# All arcs retain arrowheads.
# Orange arcs form the directed shortest path:
# A -> B -> C -> E -> D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_directed_path <- ggraph(
  g_directed,
  layout = "manual",
  x = xy[, 1],
  y = xy[, 2]
) +
  
  # All directed edges in grey
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "grey75",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    arrow = arrow(
      type = "closed",
      length = unit(3.5, "mm")
    ),
    start_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    ),
    end_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    )
  ) +
  
  # Directed shortest-path edges in orange
  geom_edge_link(
    aes(
      filter = on_shortest_path
    ),
    colour = "#D95F02",
    linewidth = 1.8,
    arrow = arrow(
      type = "closed",
      length = unit(3.5, "mm")
    ),
    start_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    ),
    end_cap = circle(
      5.5,
      "mm"
    )
  ) +
  
  # Vertices
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  
  # Vertex labels
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4
  ) +
  
  coord_equal(
    xlim = x_limits,
    ylim = y_limits,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.30)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Directed graph",
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      colour = "#D95F02",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Combine the plots side by side
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_shortest_paths <- p_undirected_path +
  p_directed_path +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 1
  )

p_shortest_paths
```


## Connectivity-based taxonomy

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the common vertex set
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vertices <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "B", "C", "D")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define one fixed layout
#
# The same vertex positions are used in all four graphs.
#
#     A       B
#
#     C       D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

xy <- matrix(
  c(
    0, 1,  # A
    1, 1,  # B
    0, 0,  # C
    1, 0   # D
  ),
  ncol = 2,
  byrow = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create an empty graph
#
# Four vertices and no edges.
# All vertices are isolated.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_empty <- make_empty_graph(
  n = 4,
  directed = FALSE
)

V(g_empty)$name <- vertices$name

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Create a disconnected graph
#
# Two connected components:
#
# A -- B
# C -- D
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_disconnected <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = data.frame(
    from = c("A", "C"),
    to   = c("B", "D")
  ),
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create a connected graph
#
# A -- B -- D -- C
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_connected <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = data.frame(
    from = c("A", "B", "D"),
    to   = c("B", "D", "C")
  ),
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Create a complete graph K4
#
# Every pair of distinct vertices is connected.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_complete <- make_full_graph(
  n = 4,
  directed = FALSE,
  loops = FALSE
)

V(g_complete)$name <- vertices$name

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Define a function for consistent plotting
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_graph <- function(graph, graph_title, graph_subtitle) {

  # Start with the graph and fixed manual layout
  p <- ggraph(
    graph,
    layout = "manual",
    x = xy[, 1],
    y = xy[, 2]
  )

  # Add edges only when the graph contains at least one edge.
  # This avoids problems for the empty graph.
  if (ecount(graph) > 0) {
    p <- p +
      geom_edge_link(
        colour = "grey65",
        linewidth = 1.1
      )
  }

  # Add vertices, labels, and common formatting
  p +
    geom_node_point(
      size = 9,
      shape = 21,
      fill = "#DCEAF6",
      colour = "#2C6E9F",
      stroke = 1.1
    ) +
    geom_node_text(
      aes(label = name),
      size = 4
    ) +
    coord_equal(
      xlim = c(-0.20, 1.20),
      ylim = c(-0.20, 1.20),
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = graph_title,
      subtitle = graph_subtitle
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 13,
        face = "bold",
        hjust = 0.5
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 10,
        colour = "grey35",
        hjust = 0.5,
        margin = margin(b = 5)
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(
        b = 5,
        l = 5,
        r = 5,
        t = 5
      )
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Create the four plots
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_empty <- plot_graph(
  graph = g_empty,
  graph_title = "Empty graph",
  graph_subtitle = "No edges"
)

p_disconnected <- plot_graph(
  graph = g_disconnected,

p_connected <- plot_graph(
  graph = g_connected,

  graph_title = "Complete graph",

)

p_taxonomy <- (

## Star graph

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function for creating and plotting a star graph K_{1,n}
#
# n_leaves = number of pendant vertices
# Total number of vertices = n_leaves + 1
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_star_graph <- function(n_leaves) {
  
  # Create the star graph:
  # vertex 1 is the central vertex
  # all remaining vertices are pendant vertices
  g_star <- make_star(
    n = n_leaves + 1,
    mode = "undirected",
    center = 1
  )
  
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Construct a circular layout
  #
  # The central vertex is at (0, 0).
  # The pendant vertices are distributed evenly around it.
  # The first pendant vertex is placed at the top.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  
  angles <- seq(
    from = pi / 2,
    to = pi / 2 + 2 * pi,
    length.out = n_leaves + 1
  )
  
  xy <- rbind(
    
    # Central vertex
    c(0, 0),
    
    # Pendant vertices
    cbind(
      cos(angles[2:(n_leaves + 1)]),
      sin(angles[2:(n_leaves + 1)])
    )
  )
  
  # Mathematical label below the graph
  graph_label <- bquote(
    K[1 ~ "," ~ .(n_leaves)]
  )
  
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Plot the star graph
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  
  ggraph(
    g_star,
    layout = "manual",
    x = xy[, 1],
    y = xy[, 2]
  ) +
    geom_edge_link(
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    geom_node_point(
      size = 5.5,
      shape = 21,
      fill = "black",
      colour = "black",
      stroke = 0
    ) +
    coord_equal(
      xlim = c(-1.20, 1.20),
      ylim = c(-1.20, 1.20),
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(
      caption = graph_label
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 18,
        colour = "black",
        hjust = 0.5,
        margin = margin(
          t = 5
        )
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(
        t = 10,
        r = 8,
        b = 5,
        l = 8
      )
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create the sequence of star graphs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_star_3 <- plot_star_graph(
  n_leaves = 3
)

p_star_4 <- plot_star_graph(
  n_leaves = 4
)

p_star_5 <- plot_star_graph(
  n_leaves = 5
)

p_star_6 <- plot_star_graph(
  n_leaves = 6
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine the four graphs horizontally
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_star_sequence <- (
  p_star_3 |
  p_star_4 |
  p_star_5 |
  p_star_6
) +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 4,
    widths = c(1, 1, 1, 1)
  )

## Trees

```{r}

# Helper function for creating a tree plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_tree <- function(edges, vertices, coordinates, label) {
  
  # Create the undirected tree
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(
    d = edges,
    directed = FALSE,
    vertices = data.frame(name = vertices)
  )
  
  # Match coordinates to the internal vertex order
  coordinates <- coordinates[
    match(V(g)$name, coordinates$name),
  ]
  
  # Verify that the graph is a tree
  stopifnot(is_tree(g))
  
  # Plot
  ggraph(
    g,
    layout = "manual",
    x = coordinates$x,
    y = coordinates$y
  ) +
    geom_edge_link(
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    geom_node_point(
      size = 5.5,
      shape = 21,
      fill = "black",
      colour = "black",
      stroke = 0
    ) +
    coord_equal(
      xlim = c(-1.8, 1.8),
      ylim = c(-0.30, 2.30),
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(
      caption = label
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 18,
        colour = "black",
        hjust = 0.5,
        margin = margin(t = 7)
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(
        t = 10,
        r = 8,
        b = 5,
        l = 8
      )
    )
}

## planar graph

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the graph
#
# The graph is the cycle graph C5, drawn first as a five-pointed
# star and then as a crossing-free pentagon.
#
# Edge sequence:
#
# A -- C -- E -- B -- D -- A
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Intersections between star edges are not vertices.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vertices <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
)

edges <- data.frame(
  from = c("A", "C", "E", "B", "D"),
  to   = c("C", "E", "B", "D", "A")
)

g_star <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = edges,
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = vertices
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create coordinates for five positions on a circle
#
# Position 1 is at the top.
# The other positions proceed clockwise.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

angles <- pi / 2 - 2 * pi * (0:4) / 5

circle_positions <- data.frame(
  position = 1:5,
  x = cos(angles),
  y = sin(angles)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Layout 1: five-pointed star drawing
#
# Vertices are assigned around the circle in alphabetical
# order:
#
# Position 1: A
# Position 2: B
# Position 3: C
# Position 4: D
# Position 5: E
#
# Because the edges connect every second position, the
# resulting drawing is a five-pointed star.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

layout_star <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  x = circle_positions$x,
  y = circle_positions$y
)

# Match coordinates to the internal igraph vertex order
layout_star <- layout_star[
  match(
    V(g_star)$name,
    layout_star$name
  ),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Layout 2: crossing-free planar drawing
#
# The vertices are placed around the circle in edge order:
#
# A, C, E, B, D
#
# The graph is unchanged. Only the vertex positions change.
# The same edges now form a pentagon without crossings.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

planar_order <- c("A", "C", "E", "B", "D")

layout_planar <- data.frame(
  name = planar_order,
  x = circle_positions$x,
  y = circle_positions$y
)

# Match coordinates to the internal igraph vertex order
layout_planar <- layout_planar[
  match(
    V(g_star)$name,
    layout_planar$name
  ),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot 1: star-shaped drawing with crossings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_star <- ggraph(
  g_star,
  layout = "manual",
  x = layout_star$x,
  y = layout_star$y
) +
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25),
    ylim = c(-1.20, 1.25),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Star-shaped drawing",
    subtitle = "Edges cross, but crossings are not vertices",
    caption = expression(C[5])
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      colour = "grey35",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 5)
    ),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 17,
      colour = "black",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(t = 6)
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 8,
      r = 8,
      b = 5,
      l = 8
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot 2: crossing-free planar drawing
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_planar <- ggraph(
  g_star,
  layout = "manual",
  x = layout_planar$x,
  y = layout_planar$y
) +
  geom_edge_link(
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 9,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#DCEAF6",
    colour = "#2C6E9F",
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    size = 4.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25),
    ylim = c(-1.20, 1.25),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Crossing-free drawing",
    subtitle = "A planar embedding of the same graph",
    caption = expression(C[5])
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      colour = "grey35",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 5)
    ),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 17,
      colour = "black",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(t = 6)
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 8,
      r = 8,
      b = 5,
      l = 8
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Combine both drawings horizontally
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_star_planarity <- (
  p_star |
  p_planar
) +
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 2,
    widths = c(1, 1)
  ) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Two drawings of the same planar graph",
    subtitle = "E = {{A,C}, {C,E}, {E,B}, {B,D}, {D,A}}",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 16,
        face = "bold",
        hjust = 0.5
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 11,
        hjust = 0.5,
        margin = margin(b = 8)
      )
    )
  )

p_star_planarity

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Verify that the graph is C5 and is planar
# ------------------------------------------------------------

as_edgelist(
  g_star,
  names = TRUE
)

degree(g_star)
# Every vertex has degree 2

is_connected(g_star)
# TRUE




```


## Bridges of Königsberg problem

```{r}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the four land masses
#
#              C
#       Northern riverbank
#
#              A                 D
#       Kneiphof island      Lomse island
#
#              B
#       Southern riverbank
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vertices <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  land_mass = c(
    "Kneiphof island",
    "Southern bank",
    "Northern bank",
    "Lomse island"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define the seven bridges
#
# There are:
#   2 bridges between A and C
#   2 bridges between A and B
#   1 bridge  between A and D
#   1 bridge  between C and D
#   1 bridge  between B and D
#
# Therefore:
#   d(A) = 5
#   d(B) = 3
